pageCache.pageTitle: The Mall School | Independent Prep School in Twickenham
pageCache.text:
The Mall School
Welcome to The Mall School. We are a proudly academic school with excellent 11+ results, promoting ambition, achievement and authenticity in our children through genuinely small class-sizes. Our rigorous curriculum, state-of-the-art facilities and enriching learning environment help children become confident, articulate and compassionate young citizens.
Alongside academic excellence, our outstanding co-curricular programme, in-house swim school and wide-ranging enrichment opportunities ensure pupils flourish throughout the school day, while curiosity and humour remain central to developing our children’s character, fit for a modern education.
Follow The Mall online
Thank you to everyone who joined us for our Open Morning last week. Visiting families joined the whole school for assembly with Mr Gosden, before our Year 5 and Year 6 children took them on a tour. No two tours were quite the same, giving parents the chance to see The Mall through the eyes of those who know it best. 👀We had such a great response that we’re adding another Open Morning – this time with breakfast cooked by our school leadership team! Young families can also join Mr Selby, our Reception teacher, for an afternoon of Festive Fun in late November.🍳 Open Morning + Breakfast – Friday 13 November 8.30am🎄 Festive Fun – Friday 27 November 1.30pm🌐 Visit our website or email admissions@themallschool.org.uk to book your place, or get in touch any time to arrange a personal tour with Mr Gosden. ... See MoreSee Less

📖 National Poetry Day at The Mall 📖The whole school got involved in National Poetry Day today, bringing poetry to life through art, performance, dance, music – and even a little French.Reception worked together to create an acrostic poem about all the things they love in class, while Year 1 explored poetry through percussion 🥁 and Year 2 wrote rich, descriptive autumnal poems. 🍂 Year 3 brought The Pied Piper to life, Year 4 performed poems about witches and Year 5 went one step further – learning a poem about a naughty witch in French! Poetry popped up across the curriculum too, from exploring Holst’s Planets Suite to expressing movement and ideas through gymnastics. 🤸And in Year 6, poetry opened up an important conversation in PSHE about the impact of bullying and how we can help each other to ‘sort it together’. A busy day of words, rhythm, movement, performance and plenty of imagination. ✨#NationalPoetryDay #Creativity #Wonder

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Ethos | Day school for children, Twickenham | The Mall School
pageCache.text:
Our Ethos
Our mission
As a co-educational preparatory school in Twickenham, we believe all children should be inspired with a lifelong love of learning. Our mission is to create an environment that sparks the love of learning in children through passion, joy, confidence and happiness. We will achieve this by providing a supportive community and place to grow, where everyone has a voice.
At The Mall, we develop true potential in all our pupils, whether it is academic, sporting, musical, dramatic or artistic. We guide all children to develop their natural curiosity and independence, leading to happy, confident individuals with a lifelong love of learning.
Our values
We embrace our differences.
Our Headmaster’s approach
The school is founded on the principles of hard work and reward through achievement, recognising milestone moments and points for reflection in our pupils’ learning. Well-roundedness is at the core of the school, and whilst no pupil can be the best at everything, they recognise each other’s abilities and celebrate their differences with confidence.
The Mall seeks to actively challenge our pupils in the areas that matter to them and the school community. Developing character and personal values which align to the school and its families is crucial. They allow children to have personal, local and global views and share them with pride. Similarly, the children will develop empathy and excellent communication skills as well as a positive work ethic, whilst knowing how to enjoy their learning and living the ‘life of education.’
We love it. The teachers are awesome. The ethos is wonderful. The kids are lovely and the parents are welcoming. It has a nurturing and supportive environment which we really needed, and which has hugely benefitted our daughter.
Beyond the classroom

pageCache.pageTitle: Headmasters Welcome | Private School | The Mall School
pageCache.text:
Headmaster’s Welcome
With a long-standing reputation and history for achieving excellent results, The Mall School offers something unique to its pupils. The school is relatively small, offering a supportive and nourishing environment in which children have their own voice, where teachers know each child and family well. Yet, we pack a punch. In lessons, on the sports field, in the arts and in areas like personal development, our pupils thrive and achieve excellence. Couple this with outstanding facilities from our pool, theatre and sports hall, purpose-built classrooms and excellent outdoor spaces, pupils experience the very best of both worlds – smallness and greatness.
The school is founded on the principles of hard work and reward through achievement, recognising milestone moments and points for reflection. Well-roundedness is at the core of the school, and whilst no pupil can be the best at everything, they recognise each other’s abilities and celebrate their differences with confidence.
“Pupils are motivated by the well-planned curriculum that focuses on academic subjects, such as English, mathematics, science and humanities, as well as emphasising creativity and problem-solving. The breadth of opportunity leads pupils to develop their knowledge, skills and understanding across a range of areas.” ISI Report, 2025
The world around our children at best is exciting, ever-changing and vibrant. However, it is equally demanding of their needs now and in the future and The Mall seeks to actively challenge our pupils in the areas that matter to them and to the school community. Developing character and personal values which align to the school and its families is crucial. This allows children to have personal, local and global views and share them with pride. In turn, they will develop skills to tackle the binary views we regularly see in society with a more nuanced and empathetic approach. Pupils have excellent communication skills, agency and work ethic, whilst knowing how to enjoy their learning and living the ‘life of education’.
“Pupils discuss and start to examine their aspirations for the future and to think about the personal qualities required to achieve their goals.” ISI Report, 2025
The Mall opened its Nursery in 2023 and it is already at capacity. The move to co-ed is well underway, which is testament to the school’s agility and boldness to make great strides. I am excited to be the Headmaster in the school’s next phase of its journey.
Above all, I believe in curating authentic and purposeful relationships with the community: parents, staff and pupils alike; to intentionally work together to provide the very best in a modern and agile independent education for all.
I am a family man, my wife Niva is a speech therapist, and my two youngest boys attend the nursery and the prep school.
I believe in building relationships throughout and beyond your admissions process. If you would like to join me for a personal tour or have tea after you have attended one of our open mornings, I would be happy to meet you.
Sam Gosden, Headmaster

pageCache.pageTitle: About Us | Co-ed Prep School, Twickenham | The Mall School
pageCache.text:
About Us
The Mall is a co-ed independent school and nursery for children aged 6 months to 11 years. In September 2023, the first girls joined the school in Reception and the move to co-education will be completed across all year groups by September 2028. View our co-ed timeline for the progress we’ve made.
Pupils benefit from our broad and creative curriculum and dedicated preparation for 11+ examinations, within a nurturing environment. Children flourish in our impressive facilities including an indoor heated swimming pool, purpose-built theatre, creative and performing arts centre, music department housing a wide range of instruments and multi-use sports hall.
The Mall achieves extraordinary results, despite being a non-selective school, thanks to our inspiring teaching and pastoral care. Our academic results speak for themselves, with our most recent cohort of leavers going on to a range of outstanding secondary schools.
The school received extremely positive feedback in all areas in its most recent ISI Inspection.
Leaders ensure that there is an effective programme for older pupils to reflect on their lives beyond school. Pupils discuss and start to examine their aspirations for the future and to think about the personal qualities required to achieve their goals.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music | Preparatory School, Middlesex | The Mall School
pageCache.text:
Music
Music is a powerful, unique form of communication that can change the way pupils feel, think and act. It brings together intellect and feeling and enables personal expression, reflection and emotional development. As an integral part of culture, past and present, it helps pupils understand themselves and relate to others, forging important links between the home, school and the wider world.
The teaching of music develops pupils’ ability to listen and appreciate a wide variety of music and to make judgments about musical quality. It encourages active involvement in different forms of amateur music making, both individual and communal, developing a sense of group identity and togetherness. It also increases self-discipline and creativity, aesthetic sensitivity and fulfilment.
Beyond the classroom

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care | Independent School | The Mall School
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
Breakfast Club and Before School Club
Breakfast Club is open to pupils to all year groups between 7:30 – 8:00am, offering a range of cereal, fresh fruit, yogurt and fruit juices.
The Before School Club is available from 8:00 – 8:15am every morning to children in Reception to Year 2, and from 8:00am pupils in Year 3 – 6 are supervised in the senior playground.
Both clubs operate on a drop-in basis and are located in the Art Room. Pre-booking is not required.
Current charges
From 8:00am, children in Years 3 – 6 are supervised in the senior playground.
Families with an older child in Year 3 to 6 may take their younger child to the Before School Club in the Art Room from 8:00am free of charge.
After School Club
The After School Club is based in the Art Room, giving children supervised access to puzzles, art activities and educational games. After School Club operates on a drop-in basis and no booking is required in advance.
Reception and Year 1 are able to attend the After School Club between 3:00 – 6:00pm.
Pupils in Years 2 and 3 can attend between 3:30 – 6:00pm.
Current charges
Homework and After School Club for senior pupils
A homework club is available to children in Years 4 to 6 between 4:00 – 6:00pm, giving pupils the opportunity to complete homework under teacher supervision. A small snack is provided [4:00-5:00pm] and high tea is provided at 5:00pm for those children staying to join the After School Club, which runs from 5:00 – 6:00pm. Homework Club operates on a drop-in basis and does not require booking in advance.
Current charges
Co-curricular Clubs combined with wraparound care
If your child is booked to attend a co-curricular club at school, and you’d then like them to go on to After School or Homework Club, one of the teachers will accompany them.
Email enquiries for any clubs or wraparound care to our School Administrator

Maths
Children at The Mall achieve a very high standard in Maths. Our aim is to develop their oral, written and practical mathematical understanding, knowledge and skills in a manner which develops confidence and enjoyment of the subject. We want children to develop a feel for numbers, to make estimations, perform calculations and to understand the significance of the results obtained. We teach them the skills necessary to solve mathematical problems by reasoning logically and to interpret their results. Through a high quality curriculum, we provide pupils with a foundation which prepares them for the further study of mathematics and related disciplines.

pageCache.pageTitle: 11+results & future schools | Destinations | The Mall School
pageCache.text:
11+results & future schools
Leavers’ Destinations 2026
Enormous congratulations to our Year 6 pupils who have, again, have achieved fantastic 11+ results. As well as being offered places at a wide range of senior schools, including some of the most academically selective locally, The Mall pupils have also been awarded numerous scholarships.
Future destinations at 11+
In 2026, Mall pupils were offered 90 places altogether. 76% of pupils received at least two senior school offers with nearly half (48%) of pupils offered places at three or more schools. 41% of pupils sitting independent senior school exams have been awarded academic, music, art or sports scholarships from schools including:
Halliford School
Hampton School
King’s College School, Wimbledon
Reed’s School
St James School
Tiffin Grammar
11+ Exam Preparation
The Mall has an enviable track record in preparing pupils for successful entry to senior schools in the highly competitive London market.
We help pupils prepare for 11+ exams on paper and on screen, encouraging regular use of online revision to support pupils with navigating computer systems similar to the ones used in 11+ exams. In the autumn term of Year 6, every child in the year group practices school interviews with the senior leadership team. It is an encouraging, fun experience and helps them to prepare well.
Finding the right school for your child
There is no such thing as the right school, only the right school for the individual child. We work with parents to identify possible schools for their child and the Headmaster will begin discussions from Year 4. Parents are invited to a series of future schools events where they learn about the application and entrance process, as well as how the school supports them and their children.
Parents can meet admissions and senior staff from a wide range of independent senior schools at our annual senior school fair in the spring term.
Our overall aim is to prepare pupils academically and socially so they can move on confidently to their next school and flourish.
Parent praise for the transition process
Parents value the support and guidance that they and their children receive from the school throughout the 11+ process.
The teaching is great and my son has made excellent progress. His senior school is perfect for him and we were well advised regarding application.
Beyond the classroom

pageCache.pageTitle: ISI Reports | Independent Prep School | The Mall School
pageCache.text:
ISI Reports
“Pupils are motivated by the well-planned curriculum that focuses on academic subjects, such as English, mathematics, science and humanities, as well as emphasising creativity and problem-solving. The breadth of opportunity leads pupils to develop their knowledge, skills and understanding across a range of areas.”
In March 2025, we were visited by the Independent Schools’ Inspectorate (ISI) which was conducted under the ISI’s new framework. A significant change in the framework is that independent schools no longer receive a single-word judgement or result such as ‘outstanding’ or ‘excellent’ to describe the outcome of the inspection. The report will more simply state if standards were ‘met’ or ‘unmet’.
You will see from our inspection report summary that there are substantial remarks that speak to the success of The Mall School as being a safe, industrious and caring environment, where relationships are at the core of our focus. It is clear from the report that staff and pupils alike enjoy the bustle and energy in the school to develop themselves and thrive.
“Pupils discuss and start to examine their aspirations for the future and to think about the personal qualities required to achieve their goals.”
Congratulations from the headmaster
Our headmaster, Sam Gosden congratulated the whole school community: “I would like to extend my thanks to the excellent staff at The Mall for their ongoing commitment to giving all pupils the best possible experience, and also to the pupils and their parents for being part of such a fantastic and supportive community, all of which has contributed to achieving this inspection outcome.”
To read the full report, or any from previous years, please click on the links below.
How are independent school in England inspected?

pageCache.pageTitle: Our History | Independent Prep School | The Mall School
pageCache.text:
Our History
The Mall School was founded in 1872 and moved to its present site in 1909. The original house was destroyed by fire in 1960, leaving only the old stable block, which housed the junior activity room and the art room.
1970 – 1986
Temporary accommodation was erected to keep the school going. More buildings were added over the years, notably by Peter Waterfield, who became Headmaster in 1969. At that time, the school buildings – but not the land – were owned by the Headmaster. When Mr Waterfield approached retirement, he handed over the school to an educational trust which was established in 1986. An appeal successfully raised over £200,000 to secure the freehold of the land.
Developments in the 1990s
A major redevelopment programme began in 1990 with the opening of the Waterfield Building, a junior block of six classrooms. The Ellis Building, a matching senior block of nine classrooms, opened in 1992. In September 1993, the Hamblin Building was also completed – it comprised a kitchen, dining room, library and staffroom. The school celebrated its 125th anniversary with the opening of the Thistlethwaite Building for Science and Music in 1997, which completed the fourth side of the inner quadrangle. Well-known sports presenter and ex-footballer, Gary Lineker opened the indoor swimming pool in July 1999.
A new building for younger pupils
In December 2000, the school bought The Old Vicarage at 84 Hampton Road to house Reception and Year 1. The building opened for the Reception classes in September 2002, with Year 1 added a year later. In September 2010 a Creative and Performing Arts Centre for drama, art and design technology was completed, as well as a new sports hall which the ex-England cricketer Angus Fraser opened in January 2014.
During August 2015 we redeveloped the science area to the rear of the Ellis building to create an outdoor classroom with a fabulous Science Garden, greenhouse and pond. In August 2016, the dining hall and kitchen were refurbished alongside a new outdoor area at Mall Infants.
Changes to the pupil cohort
In April 2017, the school announced that it was moving to 11+ and so, at the end of the summer term 2020 the last cohort of 13+ boys left The Mall.
Adapting to a global pandemic
When the worldwide pandemic forced the nation into lockdown, the school adapted its approach to teaching by providing online learning.
At the time, parents of children in Years 4 and 6 wrote to the school, with positive feedback about how quickly the teaching had been changed:
We just wanted to drop you a line to say a big thank you for delivering such a successful return to home schooling this week. It’s very clear a considerable amount of time, thought and effort has gone into making this work as best as it can for all, which has certainly come through in abundance this week given the success of the online teaching and related content. It’s certainly made our job as parents much easier and allows us to focus on supporting the children where we can be of greater benefit to them during the day.
Journey to co-education
The Mall Nursery opened in 2023 at 84 Hampton Road and OFSTED rated it Outstanding in December 2024!
We welcomed girls into Reception from September 2023 and the move to co-education, which is being phased in gradually, will be completed across all year groups by September 2028. View the timeline so far.
Beyond the classroom

pageCache.pageTitle: Private Day Nursery in Twickenham | The Mall School
pageCache.text:
The Mall Nursery
Our private day nursery in Twickenham opened at 84 Hampton Road, a few minutes’ walk from the main school site, in September 2022. In December 2024, it was rated Outstanding by OFSTED, making it one of the most highly regarded nurseries in the Richmond and Middlesex area.
Our approach is all about learning through play, following your child’s interests and using natural, authentic resources. The nursery is a vibrant, safe and stimulating environment with a family-oriented atmosphere, where children become confident, happy and independent learners.
Helping with your work-life balance
Our core opening hours are 7:30am – 6:30pm. We offer an early start from 7:00am and extended pick-up time of 7:00pm (by request) to meet the needs of busy working parents.
Situated close to several train stations, the nursery is ideal for commuters who may need to get into London and families travelling from across Richmond upon Thames and the wider Middlesex area, and our buggy park offers a convenient storage option for families.
Nursery facilities
The Mall works alongside Toddleworld Nursery Management and has created a vibrant, exciting and inspiring environment for young children. The nursery building is high-quality, bright and airy with a large outdoor space for the children to play and learn in.
The nursery children also use the school’s extensive facilities including our heated indoor swimming pool and 160-seat theatre, and draw on expertise from the school’s specialist teaching staff to enrich the Early Years Curriculum.
Progression to Reception
Children at The Mall Nursery are offered a place in our Reception class. They benefit from the familiarity of the The Mall School environment and having friends move on with them. All children in the pre-school year of the nursery will benefit from an excellent transition programme to get them ready and excited for their next school.
Find out more about the nursery including opening hours, curriculum, opportunities for play and forthcoming information events at The Mall Nursery website.
If you would like to register your interest in The Mall Nursery please complete the form and a member of staff will be in touch to arrange a visit or answer any of your questions.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pre-Prep Curriculum | Independent School, Twickenham | The Mall School
pageCache.text:
Reception & Year 1 Curriculum Guide
Reception and Year 1 classes at The Mall School provide a warm, caring and nurturing introduction to school life. Children are encouraged to explore, investigate and learn through a balance of adult-led and child-initiated activities. Children are given opportunities to develop their own learning through free-flow play both in the classrooms and in our outdoor learning environment. The curriculum is enhanced by specialist teaching in swimming, music and PE.
Reception
In Reception, the curriculum is based on the Early Years Foundation stage (EYFS) which emphasises the importance of fostering positive relationships and adapting the provision to meet the needs, interests and learning styles of each child.
At the heart of all teaching and learning is the Personal, Social and Emotional Development of each child. Alongside this, we promote pupils’ communication and language skills, their physical development and their literacy and mathematical development.
We teach in a style that will stimulate interest – pupils play, explore and investigate and are encouraged to persevere; any learning difficulties encountered are seen as learning opportunities and children are encouraged that their effort counts. Exciting topic work fosters a growing understanding of the world around them.
We work closely with parents as the partnership between school and home forms the foundation of successful, positive learning. There is daily contact with parents, both formally and informally, and parents are encouraged to take an active part in school life – through attending events and, for example, participating in our weekly ‘Share A Story’ sessions.
Children leave Reception with a positive, ‘can do’ attitude to learning and they are equipped with the confidence, knowledge and skills needed for the challenges of Year 1.
Year 1
In Year 1, children experience a more formal, although equally stimulating environment. English and Mathematics continue to have priority, although much is taught in a cross curricular approach. Practical work using Numicon in Maths or phonics games in English continue to excite the pupils’ learning. We follow our own curriculum, promoting high levels of achievement and effort and celebrating children’s successes as they acquire key skills.
In Year 1, emphasis is on key knowledge and skills in English and Mathematics and reading is given high priority with pupils and teachers selecting a new book each day from our extensive range. The partnership with parents continues and regular homework in spelling and linked to classwork is set each week.
Pupils are taught through half-termly topics, each focusing on history, geography or science. Topics are carefully chosen to both appeal to and challenge the children and include Space, The African Savannah and The Great Fire of London. Again, emphasis is placed on exploring and practical activity and the children enjoy a range of art and creative tasks from designing and making smoothies to producing their own knight’s shield.
Alongside work in the classroom, pupils have lessons with subject specialists in music, PE and swimming.

The Mall Nursery
Age ranges for children at the Nursery
The Mall Nursery welcomes boys and girls aged from 6 months to 4 years and is open 51 weeks a year, with an extended day to meet the needs of busy working parents in the local area.
Learning through play
The nursery is a vibrant, exciting and inspiring environment for young children within a high-quality and purpose built setting which includes a large outdoor space for the children to play and learn in. The nursery children also use the school’s extensive facilities including swimming pool and theatre and draw on expertise from the school’s specialist teaching staff to enrich the Early Years Curriculum.
Automatic places at The Mall School for Nursery leavers
Children at The Mall Nursery will automatically be offered a place in The Mall School’s Reception class. All children in the pre-school year of the nursery will benefit from an excellent transition programme to get them ready and excited for their next school.
Early years funding entitlement and reduced school fees
Early years funding will still be available for children who come to the school until the term after their 5th birthday. Depending on their birth date, this could entitle families to almost 30% discount on school fees
How to register for Nursery
If you would like to register your interest in The Mall Nursery please complete the form and a member of nursery staff will be in touch to arrange a visit or answer any questions you have.
